categories.title: Base styles
categories.intro: Tokens every other element is built from: colour, type, space, shape, elevation, layers, size and motion. Use these names, never raw values. Only brand tokens may be changed by a project.

categories.title: Text
categories.intro: Text styles with a fixed role. Choose by what the text is (a page title, a stat value), not by how big you want it.

categories.title: Form text
categories.intro: The words around a field: its label, requirement marker, help and errors. They decide whether a form is completed.

categories.title: Actions
categories.intro: Things people press. One primary action per screen; everything else is quieter.

categories.title: Inputs
categories.intro: Native form controls styled by ORCA. Native first: they work with keyboards, screen readers, autofill and phones for free.

categories.title: Icons
categories.intro: One icon set, 16px, single ink in currentColor. Icons support words; they never replace them.

categories.title: Status marks and labels
categories.intro: Small marks that state a condition or categorise an item. Status always pairs colour with a word and, where it matters, a shape.

categories.title: Identity
categories.intro: Who and what: the product's logo and favicon, and people's avatars.

categories.title: Imagery
categories.intro: Images, frames and graphics. Reserve their space, describe them, and keep text readable over them.

categories.title: Structure marks
categories.intro: Marks that organise and connect: rules, separators, focus, markers and backdrops. Plus the accessibility helpers every page needs.

categories.title: Progress
categories.intro: Feedback while something takes time. Respond within 400 ms; show progress for longer; describe the step past 10 seconds.

categories.title: Chart and graphic marks
categories.intro: The small marks charts, legends, zones and heat maps are made of. Every colour mark has a text label nearby.

categories.title: Planning inputs
categories.intro: Date, time and schedule inputs. Native pickers first: they are what people already know, on every device.

categories.title: Planning text
categories.intro: How dates, times and durations are written. Always machine-readable (`<time datetime>`) and formatted for the reader's locale and timezone.

categories.title: Planning marks
categories.intro: Marks drawn on calendars, schedules and timelines. Each state pairs colour with a shape, a pattern or a word.

categories.title: Planning icons
categories.intro: Icons for time and scheduling ideas, drawn by ORCA on the same 16px grid as the rest of the set.

categories.title: Forms
categories.intro: Fields and the small groups around them. A form field is the unit people complete: label, hint, error and control in a fixed order.

categories.title: Navigation
categories.intro: How people move between places and pages. The current location is always marked with aria-current and a shape, not only colour.

categories.title: Feedback
categories.intro: How the system tells people what happened and what to do next: alerts, callouts, toasts, dialogs, empty states and progress.

categories.title: Actions
categories.intro: Groups of actions: button groups, menus and the action sets that sit on records and rows.

categories.title: Data display
categories.intro: Ways to present records and numbers: stat cards, lists, key/value lists, cards, tables, timelines and small charts.

categories.title: Content blocks
categories.intro: Reusable blocks for products, people, posts, heroes and media.

categories.title: Identity and controls
categories.intro: Who is signed in, what a panel is, and the small controls that personalise the interface.

categories.title: Date and time pickers
categories.intro: Native date and time inputs, composed with shortcuts, ranges, time zones and a month grid. Native first: every device already knows how to pick a date.

categories.title: Planning selectors
categories.intro: Controls that choose days, repeats, reminders, periods, granularity and calendar views.

categories.title: Calendar parts

categories.title: Schedule parts

elements.name: Colour palette
elements.summary: Raw colours: a 13-step gray scale and eleven hues with nine numbered steps each.
elements.why: A small, named palette keeps colour consistent and lets semantic tokens point at known values (Practical UI C18: name raw colours separately from their uses). Generating the hues in OKLCH gives every step the same perceived lightness across hues, so a chart's series read as equally important.
when: Charts, zones, calendars and illustrations that need several distinguishable categories.
Defining a new semantic token inside ORCA itself.
how: Gray: `--orca-gray-0` (white) to `--orca-gray-1000` (black), Tangerine's values.
Hues: `--orca-{red|orange|amber|yellow|green|teal|cyan|blue|indigo|purple|pink}-{100..900}`; 100 is lightest.
For data series prefer `--orca-chart-1`…`--orca-chart-8`, which already pick contrasting steps per theme.
Text on a hue step: steps 100–400 take `--orca-text` in light themes; 600–900 take white.
avoid: Text, controls, grounds and status: use semantic tokens (`semantic-colors`) instead.
Telling two series apart by hue alone: change lightness or add a shape, label or pattern.

examples.title: Gray and one hue

law_names: Practical UI C18: Name raw colours separately from their uses
Practical UI C03: Communicate meaning beyond colour
Aesthetic–usability effect: consistent, careful visuals earn trust

elements.name: Semantic colour tokens
elements.summary: Colours named by their job: text, grounds, lines, interaction, status, actions, planning, data.
elements.why: Components written against roles (`--orca-text-muted`, `--orca-border-strong`) work in every theme without change, and every role carries a tested contrast promise (Practical UI C09, C01).
when: Every colour in every element and page.
how: Text: `text` (body, labels, headings), `text-muted` (help, meta), `text-inactive` (unselected nav).
Grounds: `bg` page, `bg-alt` set-apart region, `bg-input` fields, `bg-hover`, `bg-active` (pressed, selected), `bg-elevated` floating.
Lines: `border` decorative, `border-strong` controls, `border-weak` row separators.
Status families `info`, `positive`, `caution`, `negative`, `neutral`: the bare name for marks and text, `-bg` for tints, `-fill` for solid badges.
Actions: `primary*` (main action, green), `danger*` (confirmed destruction), `brand-strong*` (brand fill).
Pair every status colour with an icon and a word.
avoid: Choosing a token for how it looks rather than what it is for (a muted heading is still `--orca-text`).
Using `--orca-border` (decorative, 1.6:1) on a control: controls need `--orca-border-strong` (3:1).
a11y: `text` and `text-muted` hold 4.5:1 on `bg`, `bg-alt` and `bg-input` in every theme.
Known exception kept from Vanilla: `caution` as text is 3.0:1 in light; never set caution text alone.

elements.name: Brand colour and surfaces
elements.summary: The one brand colour, the fills derived from it, and the page surfaces it sits on.
elements.why: One brand colour plus neutrals is usually enough (Practical UI C07). Deriving the text-carrying fill automatically keeps any brand colour readable, moving the contrast work from the developer to the system (Tesler's law).
when: The one brand moment on a page: the top bar, the brand button, the logo mark, a highlight rule.
Re-branding a deployment: set `ORCA['BRAND']['color']` and nothing else.
how: `--orca-brand`: the colour as given, for decorative marks and 3px bars (needs only 3:1).
`--orca-brand-strong`: fills that carry text; darkened by ORCA until `--orca-brand-on` reads at 4.5:1.
`--orca-brand-strong-hover` / `-active`: hover and pressed fills, derived.
Surfaces: page `--orca-bg`, set-apart regions `--orca-bg-alt`, floating `--orca-bg-elevated`.
Set it in settings; ORCA reports any adjustment it made as a system-check warning (`orca.W001`).
avoid: More than one brand-filled element per screen (Von Restorff: emphasis loses power when repeated).
Status meaning: brand is never success, warning or error.
Links and checked controls: those use the accent colour.
a11y: Never rely on brand colour alone to show state; selection uses the accent and a shape.

elements.name: Accent colour
elements.summary: The single interactive colour: links, checked ticks, radios, switches, progress, selected days.
elements.why: One consistent action colour teaches people what they can act on (Practical UI C07); using it for every 'on' state makes selection recognisable at a glance.
when: Text links, the checked state of ticks, radios and switches, progress fills, selected calendar days, accent outlines and accent badges.
how: Use `var(--orca-accent)`; hover is `var(--orca-accent-hover)`.
Brand token: `ORCA['BRAND']['accent']` (light and paper) and optional `accent_dark`; ORCA darkens or lightens it to 4.5:1.
Text on an accent fill is `var(--orca-bg)`.
avoid: Static headings or decorative icons: action colour on non-interactive things misleads (C07).
Large fills behind long text.
a11y: Holds 4.5:1 on `bg` and `bg-alt` in every theme, so it can be used for link text.

elements.name: Themes
elements.summary: Light, dark and paper share every token name. ORCA has one appearance: Tangerine.
elements.why: Writing components once against shared names means a theme can never break a component (Postel's law: reliable output in every context). Users with light sensitivity or bright surroundings choose what suits them.
when: Always: every page supports all three themes for free.
Set `ORCA['THEME']` to `light`, `dark` or `paper` to force one; `auto` (default) follows the OS and the user's stored choice.
how: Put `{% orca_html_attrs %}` on `<html>` and `{% orca_head %}` in `<head>`.
A theme toggle is a button with `data-orca-theme-toggle`; it cycles light → dark → paper and remembers the choice.
Appearance: Tangerine only (square corners, 1.5px borders, filled fields with a bottom border, inside focus ring).
avoid: Theme-specific CSS in your own code: if something needs it, the token is missing; report it.
Pure black grounds: dark uses #262626 and #202020.
a11y: Contrast promises hold in every theme; dark lifts floating surfaces one step so elevation shows without shadows.

Practical UI C11: Build dark palettes independently
Practical UI C12: Use elevation consistently

elements.name: Fonts and type styles
elements.summary: Ubuntu Sans (variable) for everything, Ubuntu Sans Mono for code, on a fixed type scale.
elements.why: One legible sans serif with two working weights keeps the interface calm and readable (Practical UI T01, T04); a fixed scale makes hierarchy predictable (T05).
when: Every piece of text. Pick the style by role: heading, title, body, detail, label, code.
how: Heading: `--orca-type-h1`…`h6`, `--orca-type-page-title`, `--orca-type-display`.
Title: `--orca-type-title` (panel and card titles, 18/24 550).
Body: `--orca-type-body` (16/24) and `--orca-type-body-strong` (550). Bold is 550, not 700.
Detail: `--orca-type-detail` (14/20) for help, meta and timestamps; `--orca-type-label` (12/16 550) for table headers, badges, kickers.
Code: `--orca-type-code` with `--orca-font-mono`.
Numbers in tables and stats get `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (`.orca-num`).
Use as `font: var(--orca-type-body)`. Brand tokens `font_sans` / `font_mono` swap the families.
avoid: New sizes or weights in page CSS.
Weights other than 400 and 550 for interface text (thin 180/275 only for the large h2/h4 styles).
All caps for anything longer than a short label (W07).
a11y: Sizes are in rem so they follow the user's font-size setting; the root grows to 18px above 1681px.
Running text is capped at `--orca-measure` (70ch).

elements.name: Spacing scale
elements.summary: Eleven spacing steps on the 8px unit, named by their pixel value.
elements.why: A small set of spacing options removes guesswork and makes grouping visible: related things sit closer than unrelated things (Miller's law, Practical UI L08, L09).
when: Every margin, padding and gap.
how: `--orca-space-4` menu rows · `-8` icon to label, related controls, label to field · `-12` field to help text · `-16` button and input side padding, card padding, between fields · `-24` between sections · `-32` between page regions · `-48` alert text inset.
Work from the inside out: the innermost gap is smallest.
Utilities: `.orca-stack` (column, 8px), `.orca-row` (wrapping row, 8px; `.orca-row--16`).
avoid: Values off the scale (6px, 10px, 18px).
The same small gap at every nesting level: it flattens grouping.

elements.name: Borders
elements.summary: Three line weights: 1px hairline, 1.5px outline, 3px emphasis bar.
elements.why: Consistent line weights make structure readable without decoration (Practical UI S02); the 3px bar is reserved for emphasis so it keeps its meaning.
when: Hairline: rules, table header line, row separators.
1.5px: outlines of buttons, cards, alerts, tick boxes; the field bottom border.
3px: the selected tab, an alert's side bar, the focus ring, a highlight rule.
how: Width tokens: `--orca-hairline`, `--orca-border-width`, `--orca-bar`.
Colour tokens: `--orca-border` (decorative), `--orca-border-strong` (controls, 3:1), `--orca-border-weak` (rows).
avoid: Borders that box every group (Practical UI L01): use space first.

elements.name: Corner radii
elements.summary: Tangerine is square; only round marks and bar ends are rounded.
elements.why: One consistent shape language is part of the system's recognisable look (Aesthetic–usability effect); rounding reserved for round marks (radios, dots, avatars) keeps those marks distinct from boxes (checkboxes).
when: `--orca-radius-none` for every box: buttons, fields, cards, menus, dialogs, badges, tags.
`--orca-radius-round` for radios, status dots, avatars, step markers, the switch handle.
`--orca-radius-pill` for the switch track and count badges; `--orca-radius-bar` for progress tracks.
how: Use the tokens even for 0 so a future rounding change is a token change, not a hunt.
avoid: Rounding a checkbox: the square box versus round radio is how people tell one-of-many from many (Practical UI R07).

elements.name: Shadows and elevation
elements.summary: Three shadows (card, elevated, dragged) and elevation utilities. Only floating things cast a shadow.
elements.why: Depth signals what sits above the page and what can be moved (Practical UI C12, L05). Reserving shadows for floating things keeps them meaningful.
when: `shadow-card`: the hover lift of an interactive card.
`shadow-elevated`: menus, dropdown lists, popovers, toasts, drawers.
`shadow-dragged`: a dragged item, a dialog, a sidebar opened over content.
how: Utilities: `.orca-elevation-0` … `.orca-elevation-3` (2 and 3 also set `--orca-bg-elevated`).
In dark themes elevation also comes from the lighter `--orca-bg-elevated` surface.
avoid: Shadows on cards at rest, panels or page sections: use a border or `bg-alt`.

elements.name: Layers (z-index)
elements.summary: A fixed stacking order from page content to the skip link.
elements.why: A named stacking order prevents the 'z-index: 9999' arms race and guarantees, for example, that a save toast is never hidden behind a dialog (Peak–end rule: the end of an action must be seen).
when: Anything positioned that must sit above or below something else.
how: Order: `layer-base` 0 < `raised` 1 < `sticky` 10 < `sidebar` 20 < `dropdown` 100 < `drawer` 150 < `dialog` 200 < `toast` 300 < `tooltip` 400 < `skip` 1000.
Use `z-index: var(--orca-layer-dropdown)`.
avoid: Raw z-index numbers.

elements.name: Control heights
elements.summary: Five heights shared by buttons, fields, selects and toggles: sm, dense, md, lg, xl.
elements.why: Controls that share a height line up in rows and toolbars (alignment), and the 44px touch minimum is applied in one place for every control (Fitts's law, Practical UI B11).
when: md (37px) by default; dense (29px) in top bars and filter bars; sm (22.5px) inside table rows; lg (44px) for touch-first screens; xl (48px) for phone primary actions.
how: Modifiers: `--sm`, `--dense`, `--lg`, `--xl` on `.orca-button`, `.orca-input`, `.orca-select`, `.orca-icon-button`.
On coarse pointers and below 620px every control grows to `--orca-control-lg` (44px) automatically.
avoid: Mixing heights in one row of controls.

elements.name: Motion
elements.summary: Four durations and two easings, all under the 400 ms Doherty threshold.
elements.why: Fast, consistent feedback keeps people in flow (Doherty threshold). Motion explains change; it never decorates. Reduced-motion users get the end state immediately (Von Restorff accessibility note).
when: snap 0.1s: hover on buttons, tabs, rows.
fast 0.165s: field fills, chevrons, card lift.
brisk 0.333s: ticks, switches, accordions, drawers, progress.
how: `transition: background-color var(--orca-duration-snap) var(--orca-ease-in)` for hover.
`var(--orca-ease-out)` for anything arriving.
ORCA's base layer stops animations for `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
avoid: Animations longer than 0.333s on interface feedback.
Looping motion except spinners, skeletons and indeterminate progress.

elements.name: Task item
elements.summary: A task row: completion checkbox, title and chips for assignee, due date and priority.
elements.why: The checkbox is the fastest way to complete a task in place (Fitts's law); chips in a fixed order make many tasks scannable (Miller's law).
when: Task lists, checklists, project and run follow-ups.

Done: `--done` strikes the title; save immediately and offer Undo in a toast.

elements.name: Milestone item

when: Roadmaps, project overviews, milestone timelines.
how: `<div class="orca-plan-row">` with a milestone marker, `.orca-plan-row__body` (name + `__meta` date) and a status chip.

elements.name: Deadline item
elements.summary: A deadline row: flag, name, due date and how long is left or how late it is.
elements.why: Time left is what people act on (Tesler's law: compute it for them); turning amber when close and red when late, with words, prevents surprises (Peak–end rule, C03).
when: Deadline lists, compliance dates, renewals.
how: `.orca-plan-row` with the deadline marker icon, the body (name + due date) and either a due-date chip (`--soon`) or an overdue marker.

elements.name: Gantt bar
elements.summary: A task as a bar positioned on a time grid, with a progress line and milestones as diamonds.
elements.why: Seeing tasks along time shows overlaps, gaps and the critical path at a glance (Gestalt, Practical UI L03); the progress line and late outline add state without colour alone.
when: Project timelines and roadmaps.
how: `<div class="orca-gantt" style="--orca-cols: 7">` of `.orca-gantt-row`s: `.orca-gantt-row__label` and `.orca-gantt-row__lane` holding `<a class="orca-gantt-bar" style="--orca-start: 14%; --orca-span: 43%; --orca-progress: 60%">`.
Variants `--done`, `--late`; milestones are milestone markers with `--orca-start`. Wrap in `.orca-table-wrap` for horizontal scroll; offer a list view for screen readers.

elements.name: Resource row
elements.summary: A person or resource with their load and a row of day cells showing availability.
elements.why: Planners assign work by comparing who is free when; aligning every resource on the same day columns makes that comparison visual (Miller's law), and patterns plus counts avoid colour-only meaning (C03).
when: Capacity planners, rosters, resource schedulers.
how: `<div class="orca-resource-row" style="--orca-cols: 7">` with `.orca-resource-row__who` (avatar, name, `__load` '32 of 40 h') and `.orca-resource-row__slots` of spans using availability fills and hour counts.
Give each slot an accessible label ('Monday, 8 h, busy').
